examples.text: Надо всё сделать и вычесть вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and will deduct on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют вычесть.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to will deduct.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тоимость'). Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'cost / price' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я вычту стоимость из вашей зарплаты.
examples.trans: I will deduct the cost from your salary.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть стоимость.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always cost.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from/out of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Извините, а кто вообще этот человек?
examples.trans: Excuse me, and who is this person anyway?

examples.text: Сейчас это самый известный модный модельер.
examples.trans: Right now he is the most famous fashion designer.

examples.text: Я хотел купить одно из ваших платьев.
examples.trans: I wanted to buy one of your dresses.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your, yours (polite or plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Моя будущая жена ваша большая поклонница.
examples.trans: My future wife is a big admirer of yours.

examples.text: Я хотел купить одно из ваших платьев.
examples.trans: I wanted to buy one of your dresses.

examples.text: Она мечтала петь именно в вашем платье.
examples.trans: She dreamed of singing in your dress specifically.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'рплата'). Common feminine noun meaning 'paychecks' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я вычту стоимость из вашей зарплаты.
examples.trans: I will deduct the cost from your salary.

examples.text: Он живёт на зарплату.
examples.trans: He lives on his salary.

examples.text: У него хорошая зарплата.
examples.trans: He has a good salary.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Ладно, ребята, всем пока до завтра.
examples.trans: Alright, guys, bye everyone until tomorrow.

examples.text: Ладно, ребята, тогда мы с вами договорились.
examples.trans: Alright, guys, then we have a deal.

examples.text: Ладно, мы до завтра спокойно потерпим.
examples.trans: Alright, we will calmly be patient until tomorrow.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'after all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотри, веди себя тут аккуратно, хорошо?
examples.trans: Mind you behave yourself carefully here, okay?

examples.text: Ладно, ведь высокая цель оправдывает средства.
examples.trans: Alright, a noble goal justifies the means after all.

examples.text: Как же так, ведь это нечестно!
examples.trans: How can that be, that is not fair!

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'сокий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('high, tall').

examples.text: Наш ресторан претендует на высокую награду.
examples.trans: Our restaurant is a contender for a high award.

examples.text: Ладно, ведь высокая цель оправдывает средства.
examples.trans: Alright, a noble goal justifies the means after all.

examples.text: У него высокая температура.
examples.trans: He has a high temperature.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'goal' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ладно, ведь высокая цель оправдывает средства.
examples.trans: Alright, a noble goal justifies the means after all.

examples.text: У нас есть взрослая цель.
examples.trans: We have a grown-up goal.

examples.text: Какая у тебя цель?
examples.trans: What is your goal?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'justifies'.

examples.text: Ладно, ведь высокая цель оправдывает средства.
examples.trans: Alright, a noble goal justifies the means after all.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и оправдывать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and justifies on time.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'редство'). Common neuter noun meaning 'means; funds (pl)' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ладно, ведь высокая цель оправдывает средства.
examples.trans: Alright, a noble goal justifies the means after all.

examples.text: Приказ Аникеева о выделении средств остался?
examples.trans: Is Anikeev's order on allocating the funds still there?

examples.text: На строительство выделили большие средства.
examples.trans: Large funds were allocated for the construction.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Здравствуйте, буду рад видеть вас в ресторане.
examples.trans: Hello, I will be glad to see you in the restaurant.

examples.text: Витя, ты не видел мою тунику?
examples.trans: Vitya, have you seen my tunic?

examples.text: Жаль, не видно вчерашнего симпатичного бармена.
examples.trans: Too bad yesterday's handsome bartender is not around.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('yesterday's (events)').

examples.text: Жаль, не видно вчерашнего симпатичного бармена.
examples.trans: Too bad yesterday's handsome bartender is not around.

examples.text: Ты что здесь делаешь? После вчерашнего!
examples.trans: What are you doing here? After yesterday!

examples.text: Это вчерашняя газета.
examples.trans: This is yesterday's newspaper.

meanings.en: likeable, appealing (short form: он мне симпатичен = I like him / I find him likeable)
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'импатичный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('likeable, nice; cute').

examples.text: Жаль, не видно вчерашнего симпатичного бармена.
examples.trans: Too bad yesterday's handsome bartender is not around.

examples.text: Он мне симпатичен, нормальный мужик.
examples.trans: I like him, he's a decent guy.

examples.text: Симпатичная девушка.
examples.trans: A cute young woman.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'bartender' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Жаль, не видно вчерашнего симпатичного бармена.
examples.trans: Too bad yesterday's handsome bartender is not around.

examples.text: Эта модель ходила с барменом в номер!
examples.trans: That model went to a room with the bartender!

examples.text: Зачем ты не сказал, что не бармен?
examples.trans: Why did you not tell her that you are not the bartender?
